children: Rising power demand and low coal inventories at Indian power plants are poised to support Coal India's volumes and improve its earnings trajectory, Jefferies analysts Sagar Sahu and Nitij Mangal say in a note. India's coal inventories have fallen to seven days versus a 10-year average of 15 days, while higher global coal prices could also support domestic e-auction realizations. Jefferies estimates that Coal India's annualized earnings will grow 6% over FY26-FY29 following a 12% decline in FY24-FY26. Jefferies retains a buy rating on the stock with a target price of 500 Indian rupees. Shares are up 0.6% at 424.35 Indian rupees. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
